id_and_class.summary: Benjamin Libet proposes that conscious experience is a Conscious Mental Field (CMF): a unified, nonphysical field produced by the activity of very large populations of neurons and able to act back on them. He introduced it to explain why distributed, divisible brain activity yields one unified experience, and to give consciousness real causal power. Libet also designed a neurosurgical test for the field, which has never been run.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Brain-Generated Nonphysical Field

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Subjective experience is a field, a system property generated by the appropriate activity of billions of neurons, that belongs to no known category of physical field and is directly accessible only from the first-person perspective.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind and brain are independent variables that interact causally. Neurons generate the CMF and it can influence neuronal activity, but it is not a Cartesian substance and cannot exist apart from the brain.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Strong emergence (brain organization produces a nonphysical field that is irreducible to the neurons and causally effective)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: The field is the unified subjective experience itself, known only from the inside; an outside investigator learns of it only through the subject’s reports.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Libet offers no mapping from neural states to particular qualitative contents and no account of why a field should be experiential rather than merely unifying.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Neurons and their distributed activity; a nonphysical conscious mental field that is spatially coextensive with them but not detectable by physical means.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: First-person experience and subjective report, combined with intracranial stimulation studies in awake neurosurgical patients.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A single experiential field into which contributions from spatially distributed neural populations are integrated.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (unity of experience); Agency (conscious will and veto). Libet leaves cognition, memory, learning, attention, arousal, and emotion to ordinary neural processes.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Field-like integration with reciprocal causation: like a current giving rise to a magnetic field, neural activity generates the CMF, which then acts back on the neural activity. Libet stresses the analogy is structural, not physical.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: The field arises whenever appropriate multifarious brain activity occurs and depends on that activity for its existence.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Spatially coextensive with the generating neural populations across cortex, yet not a measurable physical field.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The CMF can influence neuronal function, which grounds the conscious veto that Libet defended as a genuine power over action.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity is the field’s defining attribute. Libet held that neither localization nor distributed synchrony explains why spread-out cortical activity is experienced as one.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Contributions from distributed cortex reach unified experience by field contiguity, which in principle need not travel along neural connections.
core_claims_and_evidence: Stimulating specific cerebral sites produces specific conscious contents, yet experience arrives as one unified field, a gap Libet treated as data.
Subjective experience is nonphysical, so mind and brain are independent variables that interact.
The CMF belongs to no known category of physical field, electromagnetic or otherwise.
If an isolated slab of cortex could still contribute to experience, the contribution would have to travel by field rather than neural connection.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical neurophysiology (intracranial stimulation and timing studies) combined with philosophical argument from phenomenal unity.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Proposed isolated-slab test: neurosurgically cut a cortical slab off from all synaptic connections while keeping its blood supply and stimulability, then check whether its activity still shows up in the subject’s experience. Surgical, interpretive, and ethical obstacles have kept it from being attempted.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Libet offered no account of how a nonphysical field couples to neural firing, which runs into the energy-conservation objection to interactionism. He gave no criterion for which neural populations generate the field, and physicalists can accept his first-person/third-person distinction as epistemic without accepting an ontological one. A field defined partly by its undetectability sits uneasily with the empirical discipline behind his own work.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: No mechanism for physical-to-nonphysical emergence, no instrument to detect the field, no mapping to particular qualities, and no evidence of non-neural transmission. The hard problem recurs one level up: why the field is felt at all.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: In 1994 Libet suggested the CMF might fit several mind-brain theories; by 2006 he called it plainly nonphysical. The mature view is coherent as emergent interactionism but carries that family’s standard burdens.

AI_consciousness.rationale: The field is generated by appropriate neural activity, and Libet gives no criterion for which systems produce it, so whether a machine could is left open.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since the CMF depends on neural activity for its existence and cannot exist apart from the brain, it ends when the brain does.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Libet’s defense of free will and moral responsibility gives conscious agency real weight, without any cosmic purpose.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Whether a simulation would generate the field depends on what kind of activity produces it, which Libet does not specify.
